questions.solution_text:
$f(-x) = -x^{5} = -f(x)$, so $f$ is odd and $\int_{-2}^{2} x^{5}\,dx = 0$.
The two halves have equal area, so the total area is twice the area on $0\le x\le 2$.
$2\int_{0}^{2} x^{5}\,dx$
$= 2\left[\dfrac{x^{6}}{6}\right]_{0}^{2}$
$= 2\left(\dfrac{32}{3}\right)$
$= \dfrac{64}{3}\ \text{units}^{2}$

questions.solution_text:
$-x^{3}$ and $5x$ are odd; $3x^{4}$ and $-8$ are even.
$\int_{-2}^{2}\left(-x^{3}+5x\right)dx = 0$
$\int_{-2}^{2}\left(3x^{4}-8\right)dx = 2\left[\dfrac{3x^{5}}{5}-8x\right]_{0}^{2} = 2\left(\dfrac{96}{5}-16\right) = 2\left(\dfrac{16}{5}\right)$
$\int_{-2}^{2}\left(3x^{4}-x^{3}+5x-8\right)dx = 0+\dfrac{32}{5}$
$= \dfrac{32}{5}$

questions.solution_text:
$x^{3}-16x=0$
$x\left(x-4\right)\left(x+4\right)=0$
$x=-4,\ 0,\ 4$
$f(-x) = -x^{3}+16x = -f(x)$, so $f$ is odd and the two halves have equal area.
On $0\le x\le 4$ the curve lies below the $x$-axis.
$\int_{0}^{4}\left(x^{3}-16x\right)dx = \left[\dfrac{x^{4}}{4}-8x^{2}\right]_{0}^{4} = 64-128 = -64$
$\text{Area} = 2\times 64$
$= 128\ \text{units}^{2}$
